column3: Adds a women-centered legal boundary around separation, conduct, and transgression.
Adds a general frame in which conduct follows an established disposition.
The directional language is only boundary evidence for the bodily-space reading.
Provides the immediately preceding legal transition from tested migration to responsible membership.
Sets kinship and children within accountability, qualifying the pledge's household concerns.
Offers a general mercy-and-return horizon after wrongdoing.
Adds regulated marriage, sexual restraint, and mercy within a women-centered legal setting.
Contrasts hostile hands and tongues with the pledge's accountable conduct.
Adds an arrival of a clear messenger, only indirectly paralleling the address.
Joins prophetic address with divine knowledge, forgiveness, and mercy.
Frames the demand for acceptable obedience against speech unfulfilled by conduct.
Supplies kinship and marriage boundaries alongside the pledge's sexual and household terms.
Directly joins women, manifest indecency, and conduct designated as ma'ruf.
Sets exclusive worship and disavowal as the surah's prior allegiance boundary.
The limbs material is contrast evidence, not support for a preferred bodily reading.
Adds disclosure, reconciliation, and reciprocal ma'ruf within marital relations.
States exclusive divine worship and submission, the pledge's first governing commitment.
Directly develops pledge, hand, covenant fidelity, and consequent responsibility.
The hand incident is contrast evidence and adds no relevant pledge dimension.
Supplies the surah's alignment, secrecy, and loyalty frame for communal commitment.
Pairs exclusive worship with received messenger-address, while retaining the bodily contrast boundary.
Adds obedience in a shared matter, authorized leave, and prophetic seeking of forgiveness.
Closes the surah with an allegiance boundary that contextualizes the community formed at 60:12.
Reiterates mercy but adds little beyond the already explicit closing attribute.
Qualifies parent-child ties through individual accountability without directly developing the pledge.
Adds a general warning against deviation, with no distinct pledge term.
Contributes committed practice but is remote from the women-specific undertaking.
Links return, removal of wrong, prophetic community, and forgiveness.
Reinforces the surah's prayer for forgiveness, though it is less specific than 60:12.
Makes hands and feet accountable witnesses, strongly illuminating the bodily-act reading.
Directly parallels the command that the prophet seek divine forgiveness.
Extends the neighboring legal settlement and reciprocal obligations after changed marriage ties.
Names buhtan in a hearing-and-speaking setting, directly clarifying the pledge's prohibition.
Combines exclusive worship with forgiveness for believing men and women.
Adds only mutual waiting and no discernible pledge dimension.
Provides a prior-prophet parallel, only distantly relevant to prophetic reception.
Adds mercy after wrongdoing, repentance, and repair for those who come in faith.
Supplies the surah's counterpoint of good conduct and equity across a defined boundary.
Directly links self-directed falsehood with what people fabricate.
Adds maternal care, child protection, consultation, and ma'ruf obligations.
Repeats the surah's exemplary-allegiance frame without adding a specific 60:12 term.
Adds a reception scene where truth is misclassified, only indirectly related to acceptance.
Offers household inheritance rules but no distinct contribution beyond earlier family-law cards.
Separates each party's deeds, a distant accountability parallel.
Explicitly prohibits fabrication against God, but repeats the falsehood line already established.
Adds dignified release after marriage, extending the legal care of women.
Defines the surah's contrary allegiance case against which communal commitment is situated.
Adds prophetic identity only, without a specific pledge connection.
Contributes formalized obligation and witness practice, but only through a weak parallel route.
Adds the possibility of changed relations under divine forgiveness and mercy.
Directly joins wrongful accusation of an innocent person with buhtan and manifest sin.
Adds women, sexual wrongdoing, and evidentiary procedure as a legal parallel.
Offers acceptance of the best deeds and passing over wrongs, reinforcing non-perfectionist mercy.
Adds another direct pledge scene, but is redundant after the fuller covenant card.
Adds a narrow post-marital protection rule with limited connection to the pledge.
Directly states the sexual boundary that the pledge includes among its terms.
Develops pledge as a binding exchange and fulfilled covenant, though in a different setting.
The hand reference is contrast evidence and adds no relevant pledge dimension.
Protects believing women from accusations, extending the pledge's ban on false accusation.
The feet and bodily-direction material remains contrast evidence rather than direct support.
Combines obedience to the messenger with turning back and mutual seeking of forgiveness.
Reinforces one community under one Lord and worship, behind the pledge's opening term.
The front-and-back language supplies only a contrast boundary for the bodily reading.
Combines a procedural messenger setting with forgiveness, but its route includes contrary evidence.
Adds rejection and pride without a distinct 60:12 dimension.
Directly identifies fabrication of lies, though it repeats earlier falsehood evidence.
Connects sexual violation with marriage boundaries, supplementing the zina prohibition.
Adds reciprocal action from opposed positions, not the pledge's content.
Reiterates forgiving mercy and delayed reckoning without a specific additional term.
Places buhtan within marital exchange and wrongful taking, adding a household legal instance.
Supplies a concrete killing act, extending the pledge's prohibition beyond the child-specific clause.
Reiterates divine forgiveness while its contrary route remains a boundary, not support.
Adds lawful marriage and exclusion of sexual breach, though much overlaps earlier cards.
Makes tongue, hands, and feet witnesses to deeds, reinforcing bodily accountability.
Offers only another general scene of requested forgiveness.
Reiterates seeking forgiveness with devotional practice, without a new pledge term.
Adds prophetic identity but no distinct relation to the undertaking.
Directly couples obedience with qawlan marufa, clarifying the conduct clause.
The route is provisional and contrastive, without a useful pledge contribution.
Collects exclusive worship, child protection, sexual restraint, and unlawful killing in one command cluster.
The contrary route offers no positive support for the pledge's mercy reading.
Provides a contrast between profession and truth, only indirectly relevant to receiving a pledge.
Links hands, consequences, and pardon through a provisional, nonlocalized route.
Adds arrival imagery without a discernible pledge dimension.
Shows restrained hands, but its bodily link is mixed with contrary boundary evidence.
Adds divine judgment and differentiated legal courses, broadly framing a binding communal rule.
Reiterates repentance and forgiveness with little added after earlier repair cards.
Pairs ma'ruf speech with forgiveness, but outside the pledge's obligations.
Treats hands as accountable agency, but only through a secondary bodily parallel.
Adds a bare arrival phrase without a distinct pledge contribution.
The household-access material is a tail audit card with no relevant pledge dimension.
The provisional and contrary route adds no useful relation to 60:12.
Adds child-related family allocation but no direct connection beyond the offspring term.
Directly rejects fabricated claims about God, though it repeats earlier fabrication evidence.
Adds messenger warning and consequence, only distantly related to the undertaking.
Provides a limited forgiveness parallel in a retaliation setting.
Reiterates mercy without an identifiable additional 60:12 dimension.
Reiterates praise and seeking forgiveness, with no new covenant or repair detail.
Supplies wrongful appropriation through judgment, only distantly adjacent to prohibited conduct.
The hands reference concerns production and adds no relevant bodily-accountability reading.
Directly recalls a covenant answered with hearing and obedience, closely paralleling the pledge.
Adds covenant obligations, breach, and forgiveness within a communal undertaking.
Collects indecency, unlawful killing, association, and false attribution in one prohibition frame.
Directly prohibits killing children, supplying the closest parallel to that pledge term.
Extends the life-protection term to unlawful killing more generally.
Provides an explicit covenant response of hearing and obedience.
Sets association apart from other wrongs in the horizon of forgiveness.
Directly relates obedience to the messenger with obedience to God.
Joins self-wronging with seeking forgiveness and finding God forgiving and merciful.
Repeats the association-and-forgiveness boundary with a distinct warning of going far astray.
Places believing women and men alike within accountable action and promised inclusion.
Names fabrication against God, supplementing the pledge's buhtan prohibition.
Adds repentance and repair after a property violation, specifying restorative mercy.
Directly condemns destroying children and false claims about what God has provided.
Pairs ma'ruf with prohibition of indecency and wrongful excess.
Supplies the direct legal treatment of zina omitted from the original list.
Directly addresses accusing chaste women and the evidentiary safeguard against false accusation.
Adds the spouse-specific accusation procedure, relevant to the alternative lineage reading.
Traces false-report circulation through tongues and labels it grave before God.
Adds the public spread of indecency as a boundary around sexual accusation and report.
Combines association, unlawful killing, and zina before immediately opening repentance and reform.
Makes repentance, faith, and repair a transformation of prior wrongs, sharpening the repair reading.
States the foundational prohibition of association within a parent-child address.
Addresses claimed lineage and preserves a parallel boundary for the bodily-origin reading.
States that believing men and women have no independent choice once God and messenger decide.
Names harm to believing women and men as buhtan and manifest sin.
States a broad non-despair horizon for forgiveness after transgression.
Links acceptance of repentance with pardon and divine knowledge of what people do.
Calls believers to obey God and the messenger while preserving their deeds.
